newsitem.title: USA: North Dakota fields dry out, plantings accelerate.
newsitem.headline: North Dakota fields dry out, plantings accelerate.

text.p: Excellent drying conditions accelerated planting progress in North Dakota during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop progress report.
"Substantial progress was made on small grain seeding during the week," the report said. "Planting remained well behind the 5-year-averages, but slightly ahead of last year."

Spring wheat acreage was 17 percent planted, ahead of three percent last week and 15 percent last year but behind the average of 45 percent. Wheat was one percent emerged, on par with last year but behind 18 percent for the average.
The state's barley acreage was 13 percent planted, versus 11 percent last year and 44 percent on average.
Oats were 14 percent planted, ahead of seven percent last year but lagging 41 percent on average.
Durum wheat was 11 percent planted, versus six last year and the average of 29 percent.

Throughout the major growing regions, farmers continued to make considerable planting progress and surpassed the five-year average. Sugarbeets were 75 percent planted, ahead of 15 last year and the average of 60 percent.
Pasture conditions were rated sven percent very poor, 12 poor, 28 fair, 46 good and seven excellent.
